#3316. How to Make Sure an 'Onion' Site on the Dark Web Is Legitimate

Thankfully, Tor Browser already has a cryptography-backed feature that can verify the authenticity of an onion site, by confirming whether it has end-to-end encryption and extended validation certificates. Here's how this feature works, where it falters, as well as what other red flags you should look for.

While phishing on the dark web works as it does on the clear web, scammers have a few unique advantages due to the secretive nature of the environment. Most importantly, you can’t just glance at an onion link to tell if the site is genuine. Normal website URLs tend to be short and memorable, while onion links are 56-character strings of alphanumeric text that look mostly like gibberish.

When you try to connect, Tor Browser verifies the URL against the originating website’s cryptographic key, which is how you know nobody has hijacked the address or tampered with it midway. But since this has the unwanted effect of making domains harder to recall, scammers have a much easier time generating lookalike addresses or creating website clones.

For example, many popular websites use “vanity prefixes” to make their onion addresses more easily identifiable or to add some branding appeal. That means their 56-character onion link starts with something like “facebook,” “bbcnews,” or “ciadotgov.” But scammers can use a free tool like mkp224o to generate lookalike addresses with the same vanity prefix as the legitimate website, which gives users a false sense of security.

Of course, most dark web users don’t type addresses directly into Tor Browser; they use dark web directories like the Hidden Wiki to find useful onion sites relevant to their search. Scammers will create fake search engines or link directories to point users to their fake websites, like when the Ahmia search engine discovered that a copy of its platform was directing users to 255 cloned services back in 2015.

Of course, it’s possible to orchestrate phishing attempts that don’t involve cloning sites at all. Researchers at Freie Universität Berlin describe a sophisticated technique where attackers serve the real website through their own reverse proxy, which lets them manipulate parts of the site or log your online activity without your awareness. In 2019, ESET even found a trojanized version of Tor Browser that replaced Bitcoin addresses on websites to direct payments to hackers. So both genuine websites and your browser itself are also vulnerable to manipulation if you download or access them from an unverified source.

There are a few best practices to avoid phishing attacks when using the dark web. None of them are foolproof on their own, but together, they considerably lower the risk of ending up on a fake or manipulated website.

On the desktop version of Tor Browser, you can access an onion site using a shortened version of its URL called an Onion Name. For now, this feature only works with SecureDrop, so newsrooms can establish tip lines with addresses like mysitename.securedrop.tor.onion, which would then redirect to the 56-character original onion address. This feature is in active development, so more platforms might support it in the future.

When you load up an onion site using the Tor Browser, you’ll see an onion icon on the address bar, which confirms that your connection is end-to-end encrypted. But you can also click on the onion icon to check if the site has an Extended Validation (EV) certificate, which tells you that its authenticity has been verified by a trusted certificate authority like DigiCert. While not every legitimate onion site will have an EV certificate, famous ones like Facebook tend to.

On the other hand, if you see a caution sign next to the onion icon, that means the site is using a self-signed or expired certificate that isn’t guaranteed by a trusted authority. It may also imply that the site is being served over an insecure URL. This doesn’t definitely tell you it’s a phishing site, but it’s a red flag to watch out for nevertheless.

Don’t rely on search engines, link directories, Reddit threads, or Telegram channels too heavily on the dark web. Once you’re sure you’ve found the onion address for a genuine site, bookmark it so you can access it directly the next time you want to visit.

If you realized that you’ve been the victim of a phishing attempt, the first step is to close the browser window with the fake site and access the real onion address to reset any account passwords you may have accidentally divulged.

Also, generally try to enable two-factor authentication and PGP logins on any dark web account that supports it for added security. And if you downloaded Tor Browser from anywhere other than the official Tor Project site, uninstall it now and grab a fresh copy from the official address.

#3311. Apple reportedly met with Thai officials over spyware alerts sent to politicians

Bloomberg reports that Apple has met with Thai government officials in the wake of its recent wave of iPhone alerts about mercenary spyware attacks. Here are the details.

Last week, The Financial Times and TechCrunch reported that Apple had sent a fresh wave of threat notifications to potential spyware targets in 99 countries, warning them that they may have been targeted by mercenary spyware attacks.

At the time, the FT focused on German lawmakers who had received the warnings, while TechCrunch highlighted recipients in other countries, including Beirut-based filmmaker Radwan Mortada.

Today, Bloomberg reported that “Thailand held meetings with Apple Inc. officials” over the notifications, adding that the warnings raised questions about “who may have targeted [Thai politicians] and why.”

Receiving an alert doesn’t necessarily mean a device was successfully compromised, Digital Economy and Society Minister Chaichanok Chidchob said after meeting Apple representatives Wednesday, Krungthep Turakij and other media reported. Thai authorities also have no evidence so far that the latest attempted attacks involved Pegasus, the spyware developed by Israel’s NSO Group, he said.

As Bloomberg explains, Pegasus was “allegedly used against pro-democracy campaigners in 2022.”

The recent wave of alerts, which were sent out on October 29, followed another round in August, when Apple notified potential targets in 110 countries. As always, Apple declined to disclose what triggers these notifications to prevent attackers from evading detection in the future, but recommended that recipients enable Lockdown Mode and seek expert security assistance.

Bloomberg added that Thai authorities are expected to meet with other technology companies on Thursday to discuss potential countermeasures, including risks to Android devices.

#3310. How Oz Became The Most Controversial Magazine Of All Time

Oz magazine is remembered today as one of the most notorious counterculture publications. Launched on April 1, 1963, by Richard Nevile, Richard Walsh, and Martin Sharp in Sydney, Australia, it was a satirical, psychedelic provocateur whose legal battles still feature in free-speech debates, and whose archives historians and designers now study.

Pre-Oz, Western society heavily operated on traditional post-World War II values. In other words, the status quo was staunchly conservative and rigid, with substantive dissent either intolerable or criminalised.

Staying deferential wasn’t merely a choice for the mainstream press; it was driven by routine censorship. It’s a climate that saw Britain’s Lord Chamberlain vet stage plays before they could be performed, Australian customs officials screening books and films, homosexuality outlawed, and obscenity trials happening as late as 1960.

Despite this hostility to the underground press, Oz thrived for a decade (1963-1973), and across continents. It proved that a market existed for anti-establishment satire.

The first step toward controversy is to stand out, and in media the surest way to do that is to publish what everyone else avoids. Long before Oz became famous for psychedelic London posters or the “Schoolkids” trial, it built its notorious reputation in Sydney, Australia, by printing what polite society only whispered about.

The debut April 1963 issue tackled the largely avoided subject of illegal abortion head-on, exposing underground abortion clinics and the corrupt police system that protected and profited from it. Included in the mix were incendiary takes on homosexuality, then both criminalized and deeply sensitive, along with provocations such as bodily tattoos, chastity belts, and Australia’s White immigration policy.

Oz added deadpan hoaxes that mocked public authority and symbols of sacred cultural status, such as a report of the Sydney Harbour Bridge collapsing. That was the equivalent of Parisians waking to (fake) news that the Eiffel Tower had crumbled, or New Yorkers reading on the front page of The New York Times that the Brooklyn Bridge had fallen.

If that doesn’t seem audacious enough, consider the cover of Oz’s Issue No. 6 in February 1964. It featured a photo of editor Richard Neville and two friends pretending to urinate into a newly unveiled wall fountain designed by prominent sculptor Tom Bass, a work that had just been inaugurated by Prime Minister Robert Menzies.

Oz’s early work in Sydney set the tone for its shock-and-satire identity. It also showed readers that public authorities and the mainstream press could fool them just as easily as the magazine did with its hoaxes.

Unsurprisingly, the reaction was as polarized as it was immediate. Newsstand bans did nothing to dissuade buyers who cleared all 6,000 debut copies. Establishment institutions hit back fast: advertisers pulled their contracts, writers’ jobs were threatened, and the editors were evicted from their government-owned Sydney office.

Oz had jolted Sydney’s readers, but more than 10,000 miles away in London, its 1967 relaunch as Oz London hit even harder. And it was a huge success: circulation doubled from Sydney’s 40,000 peak to 80,000 copies.

Much of the credit goes to Martin Sharp, who harnessed photographic offset lithography, freeing designers to experiment with neon colour, spiral layouts and collage. In modern terms, it was like leaping from a plain-text newsletter to a neon, meme-saturated TikTok feed.

Rather than arguing solely in neat columns as in Sydney, Oz London utilized countercultural provocations, especially with revered art and public faces. Nothing moves mouths quite like a magazine with the Mona Lisa smoking a joint, Bob Dylan as a swirling psychedelic portrait, or Vincent van Gogh as a modern hippie on its cover. That’s exactly what Oz London did.

For the average 1960s British youth, the radical art was bedroom wall poster-worthy. And a copy in hand (laden with topics such as feminism, drug laws, and the Vietnam War) became tantamount to being the cool, rebellious mind the age grade so relished.

Audacious as it was, the May 1970 issue of Oz was downright impudent. Bored with their own output, editors Richard Neville, Jim Anderson, and Felix Dennis handed the reins of an entire edition to under-18s, to test the limits of the rawness and rebellion of British adolescence. Pitch that to a modern magazine today, and the legal department would hyperventilate.

Predictably, the teenagers’ finger and mind prints were all over the resulting 48-page Issue No. 28. However, the nude cover and explicit personal ads in the back were entirely the adults' idea.

The juveniles aired their grievances, attacking the British school system’s authoritarian headmasters, corporal punishments, uniform rules, and exams. Alongside these critiques were their unfiltered views on teenage sexuality, contraception, recreational drugs, and countercultural music. Far from an orderly debate, their confrontation was chaotic and deliberately juvenile. It peaked with what is now infamously known as “The Rupert Bear incident.”

In that same issue, 15-year-old Vivian Berger made a notorious collage: she pasted the cheerful head of children's icon Rupert Bear onto a sexually explicit body of an X-rated comic by American underground cartoonist Robert Crumb, with the nursery rhymes clearly still visible underneath.

Vivian Berger’s shattering of the innocence associated with Rupert Bear (the ultimate symbol of wholesome, middle-class British childhood) was rude at best. To British authorities, though, this crossed an unforgivable line. By indulging teens in the magazine's production and publishing Berger’s explicit collage, Oz had committed cultural sacrilege in a deliberate attempt to corrupt Britain’s youth.

The police, who had hitherto restricted their raids to Oz’s offices, arrested Neville, Anderson, and Dennis and confiscated all printing materials at the Oz headquarters. This set the stage for the historic 1971 Old Bailey obscenity trial.

Anyone in London (the wider British public and International counterculture inclusive) who hadn’t heard or been bothered by Oz did so following the “Schoolkids Issue.” And the few still unbothered couldn't ignore the resulting trial that began on June 23, 1971, inside Court No. 2 at London’s Old Bailey.

This six-week trial was the longest obscenity trial in British legal history. And it was a public affair, so much so that thousands rallied in support outside the courthouse and John Lennon and Yoko Ono recorded a charity single, "God Save Us,”

Even with such a high-stakes trial, including a “conspiracy to corrupt public morals” charge that carried a life sentence, the defendants did what underground counterculture did best: mock authority. They arrived at court rocking psychedelic shirts, in schoolgirl uniforms, and having Richard Neville defend himself in court while wearing a long, flowing velvet jacket.

More importantly, it was a cultural clash between the British establishment, wielding the 1959 Obscene Publications Act under which the defendants were tried, and counterculture, represented by defendants Richard Neville, Jim Anderson, and Felix Dennis. In the end, both sides won and lost, though to varying degrees.

Neville, Anderson, and Dennis lost when they were acquitted of conspiracy but convicted of publishing and posting an obscene article, receiving sentences of 15, 12, and 9 months respectively. This was not before they were remanded for psychiatric evaluation and their signature hairs shaved.

The law’s victory was short-lived and pyrrhic. Following intense public outrage, the convictions were overturned on appeal in November 1971, and the trio walked free. Subsequently, the British justice system lost the political appetite to prosecute obscene publications, even as Oz itself buckled in 1973 under the weight of legal debt.

In the end, though, the real winner was Oz. They emerged as free-speech folk heroes whose legal victory permanently broke the back of British print censorship and paved the way for modern media freedom. Wealth flowed from it too: lessons learnt from Oz were vital in Dennis establishing a publishing empire.

#3305. Binance warns iPhone crypto holders of security flaw researchers say remains unpatched

Crypto exchange Binance has warned iPhone users about an iOS vulnerability that could allow malicious apps to access sensitive data stored by other apps. Here are the details.

In a post published on X (via AppleInsider), Binance says that a vulnerability called worse_query could allow “malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem.”

Binance says the flaw affects iOS 26.7.1, iOS 27.0.1, and iOS 27.2. However, a Community Note points out that researchers describe the vulnerability as an unpatched zero-day and that Apple’s latest security updates, including iOS 27.2.1 (the current version at the time of writing), do not mention a fix.

A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem. This is an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance.…

That said, in addition to updating their devices, Binance recommends that iPhone crypto holders take the following immediate actions:

The vulnerability was disclosed by security researchers @0xjohnny and @forcequitOS, who published a proof of concept on GitHub demonstrating how it can be used to bypass iOS sandbox protections, which normally prevent apps from accessing each other’s files.

Researcher @forcequitOS also noted that neither iOS 27.2.1 nor iOS 27.3 beta 1 patches the vulnerability.

Just as a general statement so there isn’t any confusion about it, worse_query is *not* patched in iOS 27.2.1 and 27.3 beta 1. I’ll update version support on the readme when it’s patched.

Although the researcher describes the code as intended for developers and not useful on its own, other developers have already built apps using it, including a file manager that can access, modify, and delete data belonging to other apps without requiring a jailbreak.

According to The Hacker News, neither Binance nor the researchers have reported any attacks or cryptocurrency thefts involving the vulnerability so far.

#3302. Netflix’s 8-Part Thriller Miniseries Is a Near-Perfect Binge

Tom Ripley, created by Patricia Highsmith for her novel The Talented Mr. Ripley, is one of the most iconic characters in contemporary literature. In addition to the several sequels that Highsmith wrote, Ripley has appeared in several cinematic incarnations, including the Oscar-nominated 1999 classic starring Matt Damon as the titular character. Given this storied history, making a new version of the classic story would seem like an endeavor doomed to end in disappointment. However, Netflix revamped Highsmith’s source material with the eight-episode miniseries Ripley, which saw Andrew Scott taking over the iconic role in the series by creator Steve Zaillian. Even if the story was already familiar, Ripley made creative choices that helped reframe the narrative into a twisty noir.

The character of Ripley is a true enigma who is employed by the wealthy businessman Herbert Greenleaf (Kenneth Lonergan) to find his son, Dickie (Johnny Flynn), who has disappeared in Italy with his girlfriend, Marge Sherwood (Dakota Fanning), to live a bohemian life. Although Anthony Minghella’s The Talented Mr. Ripley created a lush version of Europe that spoke to the exuberance of the post-war era, Ripley is a moody, atmospheric black-and-white drama that examines the feelings of disenchantment from expatriates. Its eight episodes allow it to expand upon details that weren’t fleshed out in some of the previous interpretations, but Ripley is such an engrossing, noir experience that it’s hard not to consume it in its entirety over the course of just one sitting.

One of the most notable differences between the original source material and Zaillian’s version is the age of the characters, who are almost two decades older than they appear in the novel. Ripley uses the faded ambitions and lack of accomplishments of its protagonists to reflect a dark side to the notion of escapism; even though Dickie has seemingly rejected his family’s responsibilities for the sake of doing his own thing, he’s revealed to be just as miserable as his father is. What makes Flynn’s version of Dickie so different than the Oscar-nominated performance by Jude Law in The Talented Mr. Ripley is that he is a vacuum of charisma who seems to have no real artistic talents, even if he engages in pretentious conversations with his friend Freddie (Eliot Sumner). This makes Ripley’s desire to literally replace him more complex; although there is still a hint of psychosexual obsession, Ripley seemingly wants to take over Dickie’s life because he feels that he could live it better.

Four Netflix characters, four completely different ways of showing up for somebody. This is the one who fits how you actually do friendship, and what having them in your life would be like.

You do not do friendship at half volume, and neither does he. What you want is somebody who says yes to the plan before you have finished describing the plan.

You are the friend who makes things happen, and so is she. Together you would be mildly exhausting to everyone around you and completely delighted with yourselves.

You have no patience for pleasant lies, and she has no ability to tell them. What looks like coldness from the outside is the most reliable friendship on this list.

You look after whoever is having the worst day. So does he. It is the least strategic way to move through the world and the best possible quality in a friend.

Ripley puts the viewer in a precarious position because the characters are as fascinating as they are repulsive. While Scott doesn’t inspire the same sense of empathy that Damon did, Ripley breaks down the senselessness of wealth, status, and etiquette by showing how shallow Dickie and Marge are. In some instances, it's darkly amusing to see Ripley disrupt their social circles and draw Dickie to a more carefree lifestyle, even if Marge wants them to settle down and have a family. There are instances in which Highsmith’s words are replicated in their entirety, but Ripley is also a masterwork in subtle audio cues that create suspense. By gradually emphasizing background noise, Ripley allows its viewers to experience the same perception of the world as its titular character does, which makes the build-up to Dickie’s murder even more suspenseful.

Even though Ripley doesn’t expand beyond the narrative of Highsmith’s first novel, the series takes the time to show the highly ornate problem-solving that Ripley faces, which makes it more believable that he’s been able to operate in obscurity. Instead of using the murder as a brief instance of a jump scare, the episode "III Sommerso" meticulously examines how Ripley lures Dickie to a place where they will not be discovered and strategizes a way to cover up the evidence. By suggesting that Ripley has planned his actions, and that they are not done out of instinctual rage, the series is able to question why he has developed these skills in the first place and why he still chose to spend so much time soaking up Dickie’s lifestyle.

While in no way does this make Ripley more likeable, at least in a traditional way, it does create a greater sense of intrigue as to how he will pull off his next scheme. There’s also a greater deal of suspense that comes from the appearance of Inspector Pietro Ravini (Maurizio Lombardi), the one member of law enforcement who seems to understand that nothing that Ripley says or admits to can be taken at face value. Ripley makes for a satisfying and conclusive experience, but there's an ambiguity to the characters that makes it even more compelling upon a rewatch.

Although it's often expressed that prestige television has replaced films as the best medium to tell mature stories for adults, Ripley is the rare series for which the description “cinematic” actually applies. Zaillian, a venerable screenwriter behind classics like Schindler’s List and American Gangster, creates a perfectly realized version of New York and Italy in the ‘60s that mirrors the stylized films that were released in the same timeframe. The film’s gorgeous look comes from Robert Elswit, the Oscar-winning cinematographer behind There Will Be Blood, who utilizes his trademark visual style that couldn’t be more distinct than the bland, oversaturated aesthetic that has become far too common within Netflix originals.

That being said, far too many Netflix shows feel like they were originally designed as movies and later extended to multiple episodes; in comparison, Ripley uses its extra running time to explore more existential questions, which are conveyed through the use of beautifully rendered flashbacks. It’s both a brilliant reconsideration for Highsmith fans and a great introduction to the world of Ripley for those unfamiliar with the material.

#3301. iPhone Duo one week later: The future, or not for me?

My iPhone Duo arrived last Thursday, so I’ve had a week to use it as my daily carry. My early experience has been mixed, so I keep asking myself an important question: is this the iPhone’s future and I just need to adapt, or is the Duo simply not for everyone?

After a week using the iPhone Duo, in some ways I have a lot of clarity about the product, and in other ways my thinking is very clouded.

To put it simply: I’m not having a great time with the Duo, which makes me wonder if the problem is me, not it.

I’ve seen countless social media posts from Duo owners proclaiming how much they love the product. And I absolutely believe them. The iPhone Duo is a remarkable innovation for the iPhone. It’s cool, weird, and wonderful in all sorts of ways. But for me and my needs (preferences?), it’s been more frustrating than enjoyable.

And that frustration mainly boils down to one thing: I almost never want to open it.

I’d estimate at least 90% of my iPhone Duo usage involves the front display. And when I unfold it the remaining 10% of the time, it’s often because I force myself to do it in the hopes of discovering what I’m missing out on. Like, I know I should be unfolding it more, so I do. But it doesn’t add any real value for me.

Because I rarely want to open the iPhone Duo, I’m left using the outer display all the time. In that mode, the Duo is too heavy for extended use, too wide to comfortably reach, and the UI in most apps is an adjustment.

Are these dealbreakers? No. I could live with the Duo’s outer display if I had to, but it’s definitely an inferior experience to my iPhone 18 Pro.

If I was opening the iPhone Duo more, and actually taking advantage of the key value proposition of foldables—that you can unfold them—I doubt the outer screen would bother me much.

But what I’ve found, at least so far, is that one-handed iPhone use is very important to me, which rules out using the inner display. I use my iPhone mostly for quick interactions, and often with a child in one hand (I have three very young kids). In situations when I do have two hands free to open the Duo, I’m probably sitting in front of my iPad Pro with a Magic Keyboard attached and would rather use the iPad instead.

So again: is the problem with the Duo, or with me?

I think foldables and slab phones will obviously coexist as there will be fans of each.

I’m absolutely already converted however and am loving my duo.

Considering the Air was my favourite phone up until this it’s surprised me. I love proper one handed use again on the outside screen and unfolded it’s much nicer than my old mini 7.

I get it’s not for everyone but those that click with it like myself have a superb device!

I think it’s the latter, but I’m not sure “problem” is the right word. I just don’t find myself using it the way it’s meant to be used. And that’s fine.

I want to love the iPhone Duo, because I see how much fun other people are having with it. And maybe given more time, something will click and I’ll start to use it “as intended.”

If iPhone Duo is the future of the iPhone, I’ll adapt and move on with my life. But one week in, I think it’s probably just not for me. And if it’s not for me, maybe there are a lot of people who will continue preferring non-foldable iPhones for many years to come.

What’s your iPhone Duo experience been like? Are you loving it or struggling? Let us know in the comments.

#3300. Netflix’s 10/10 School Drama Is The Exact Opposite Of Euphoria

The best comfort show on Netflix proves not all school dramas have to be the same. HBO’s Euphoria became a defining pop-culture phenomenon thanks to its bold take on teenage drama and its breathtaking visual style. Creator Sam Levinson injected hypnotic cinematography and Labrinth’s gospel-infused score into a tense story about addiction and growing pains, elevated by Zendaya’s Emmy-winning performance as Rue Bennett and a large cast of talented stars. Euphoria famously refuses to soften the messy realities of teens and twenty-somethings to create a sensory-heavy portrait of modern anxiety.

While not strictly the first of its kind, Euphoria is the most famous series to tackle its themes. Over a decade before Euphoria premiered, British pioneer Skins pioneered chaotic substance-fueled teen ensemble storytelling in mainstream media. Parallel to Euphoria, HBO also experimented with We Are Who We Are and Genera+ion, which explored queer youth and identity. In the years leading up to Euphoria's premiere, Netflix had already tapped into this genre. First, two years prior with the social media phenomenon 13 Reasons Why; and just a year later in 2018, with the Spanish hit Élite, which had a similar impact on Spanish-speaking audiences before Netflix expanded its reach.

It's clear that series like Euphoria strike a chord with audiences, but that doesn't mean every show with the same setting has to have a similar plot and tone.

In an era dominated by high-stress teen dramas, The Fragrant Flower Blooms with Dignity is a soothing sanctuary. Modern series like Euphoria and Élite base their edge-of-your-seat appeal on toxic relationships and psychological dread, whereas CloverWorks' adaptation of Saka Mikami's manga focuses on school students developing genuine empathy and care for each other. The plot follows the towering Chidori High student Rintaro Tsumugi, who conceals a tender heart beneath his intimidating appearance; and the petite scholarship student Kaoruko Waguri, who comes from the prestigious and rivalrous Kikyo Girls' Academy right next door. Their first meeting inside Rintaro’s family bakery sparks an immediate connection that quickly develops into wholesome love.

Instead of stretching out contrived misunderstandings and bitter love triangles, The Fragrant Flower Blooms with Dignity celebrates Rintaro and Kaoruko's honest communication. Whenever social class friction and the lingering prejudice between their rival schools threatens to pull them apart, Rintaro, Kaoruko, and their loyal circle of friends talk through their feelings and stand up for each another with remarkable grace. CloverWorks’ soft sunlit animation and expressive characters turn a remarkably low-stakes story into a pure dose of comfort television filled with mouth-watering pastries and adorable interactions.

CloverWorks’ first season of The Fragrant Flower Blooms with Dignity barely scratches the surface of Saka Mikami’s manga. Having debuted in Magazine Pocket in October 2021, the original series has grown past two hundred chapters and more than twenty collected tankōbon volumes, meaning the initial thirteen-episode anime run only covers roughly the first forty chapters, or about a quarter of the overall story. Given that Mikami’s pacing lets every emotional milestone breathe naturally, future seasons can continue adapting the manga at the exact same unhurried pace.

Netflix has some of the best romance anime series around, but only a handful are so good that they can be considered near perfect.

As the plot continues beyond the anime’s finale, Rintaro and Kaoruko’s relationship from the manga evolves into an official couple as they progress in their high school life. They eventually meet each other's families, balance part-time jobs, and confront the looming pressure of university entrance exams and post-graduation career paths. Alongside Rintaro’s own quiet growth in self-confidence and culinary passion, The Fragrant Flower Blooms with Dignity also explores their tight-knit friend groups from both Chidori and Kikyo, complete with side romances and deep bonds formed when the two once-divided worlds learn to trust each other.

Which series would you describe as your comfort show?

#3296. Gentler Streak 6.0 adds a new wellbeing timeline and customizable dashboard

In an update rolling out today, Gentler Streak is introducing new ways for users to track their wellbeing and personalize the app’s guidance based on how they feel. Here are the details.

One of my favorite exercise-tracking apps got even better today with an update that expands its functionality beyond workouts and fitness metrics to better reflect how users actually feel.

Starting today, Gentler Streak will let users log how they feel each day, including their mood, symptoms, and other factors that may not be reflected in their health and fitness data.

Some days, the way we feel isn’t reflected in what the data says, no matter the data quality. “How I Feel” captures the part that devices can’t grasp: personal context. And how you feel is not only a mood: it is also a sore throat, heavy legs or a poor night’s sleep. The feature was inspired by the Gentler Streak community, including people living with chronic fatigue, fibromyalgia, ADHD, and those not wearing their Apple Watch at night. Without overnight signals, their guidance has less to work with.

According to the team behind Gentler Streak, these new features are aimed at users whose health and fitness data may not accurately reflect how they feel, including those dealing with chronic conditions, menopause, stress, or poor sleep.

In practice, the app will now feature four tabs: Today, Health, Workouts, and Insights. In the Today and Health tabs, a new “Anything to add?” field will let users rate how they feel, from Great to Off, and add context about what might be affecting their well-being, including fatigue, feeling calm, or custom tags.

You decide when the prompt appears. Go to Profile > Settings > Self-Evaluation Prompt and choose one of three options: only when your vitals or sleep are off, always on, or never.

Gentler Stories notes that the self-assessments will override the app’s wellbeing estimates for that day, with its daily guidance adjusting accordingly.

The Today tab will also feature an expanded 10- or 30-day timeline showing logged workouts, wellbeing estimates, potential symptoms, poor sleep or vitals, and the first day of a menstrual period, while Health will introduce an interactive chart showing users how their wellbeing changes over time, with the ability to filter by symptoms.

Users can now also customize which information appears on their Today screen, including vitals, sleep, steps, menstrual cycle, VO₂ max, and workouts, which is a nice touch.

For users who are sick, injured, or taking a break from exercise, the app’s hallmark Activity Path will make way for a new Wellbeing Path, which lets them track their wellbeing on a daily basis.

For users with Active status, a new colorful wellbeing line will appear beneath the Activity Path, reflecting how they feel each day. This information is logged automatically for those who wear their Apple Watch overnight, or based on self-assessments for those who don’t.

Importantly, Gentler Stories notes that all information entered through the new feature remains on the user’s device, with no accounts or company-operated servers involved.

Gentler Streak is available for free on the App Store, with in-app purchases for monthly, yearly, family, and lifetime subscriptions.

#3292. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang set to be fired, with Johny Srouji among possible replacements [U]

Following reports of a potential second affair – this time with a subordinate – Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang looks certain to be fired by the company’s board, probably later today (though he may be allowed to ‘resign’). Apple’s chief hardware officer Johny Srouji has been listed among the potential replacements, though this seems unlikely.

Update: As we predicted, he’s gone today and Kress was indeed named interim CEO …

For anyone who’s been away from the planet for the past fortnight, Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy has been the main headline news in the tech press since it came to light at the end of last month. The New York Times broke the story on October 29, citing it then as “a close relationship.” Nvidia initially denied that the relationship was anything out of the ordinary.

That changed on November 8 when Huang publicly admitted to the affair. Nvidia’s shares dropped 5%, and the company’s board of directors opened an independent investigation. Further details emerged over the following days.

Things got even worse yesterday when the same paper reported that Huang had also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him.

It was already looking inevitable that he would be fired, and the latest revelation adds to the urgency. The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was meeting last night to discuss the CEO’s future. That future at Nvidia is likely to be measured in hours rather than days.

The board now needs to find a replacement, and Bloomberg provides a rundown on some of the potential candidates. CFO Colette Kress looks likely to head the list for at least an interim appointment. The paper names a number of other possibilities, including Apple’s chief hardware officer, Johny Srouji.

Srouji has led one of the most successful in-house silicon programs in the industry, overseeing the custom chips that power the iPhone, Mac and other Apple devices. His track record gives him deep credibility on chip design, product integration and long-term technology roadmaps. But much of his experience has been built inside Apple’s tightly controlled ecosystem, and he hasn’t been tested in the kind of high-profile salesmanship which Huang is famous for.

Given the urgency, my money is on Nvidia announcing Kress as at least interim CEO, if not a permanent replacement. It seems exceedingly unlikely that Srouji would be appointed at this time, given the in-depth negotiations and discussions that would need to take place.

As to whether he’s a potential candidate following an interim appointment, it still seems unlikely. There was an earlier report of his claimed dissatisfaction at the company, but it seems a stretch to imagine him jumping ship so soon after his promotion to chief hardware officer.

#3290. Why Apple shouldn’t worry about iPhone Duo returns

A poll of 9to5Mac readers who were lucky enough to take delivery of their iPhone Duo in the first few days shows that 30% of them have returned it for a refund.

While that could be considered bad news for the future of the device, I don’t personally consider it either surprising or worrying …

Following a report by The Verge on iPhone Duo buyers who opted to return the device for a refund within Apple’s 14-day “no questions asked” period, we thought it would be interesting to get a sense of how many people may have done this.

9to5Mac readers were always likely to have had their fingers hovering over the pre-order button for the best shot at taking early delivery, with the first of these having hit the end of the 14-day window. We ask those of you who fall into this category to tell us whether you kept or returned the device.

With close to 6,000 total votes, the results showed that close to a third of you returned your Duo.

For any other device, that would be a disastrous return rate. For the Duo, however, I don’t think it’s terribly surprising.

I voted to say I returned it just so I could see the results. I’ve never ordered nor returned an iPhone Duo.

Not providing a way to see the results without voting will have massively skewed the results. Even if the poll were better, this is a wild claim to draw from one specific, poorly assembled assembled poll.

As we noted yesterday, Apple described the iPhone Duo as “the most transformational change to iPhone since the original.” The size of that change shows up in a whole range of ways, from the weight of the device through the changed aspect ratio of the front display to a completely new way of using an iPhone.

Throw in the extremely high price tag, and I’ve always suspected that a significant number of iPhone Duo buyers would be viewing it as an experiment rather than a committed purchase. Our own Ryan Christoffel is an example of that “try it and see” attitude. One week in, he’s reached an interim conclusion that it’s probably not for him.

For those who’ve decided to return it, a number of readers shared their reasons.

“Returned it – I can’t go back to Touch ID.”

“I want to like it, but I just can’t get there. It’s awkward, and the outside screen is way too small.”

“Returned it. Not for me. I do not want to open the phone every time I want a larger screen and Apple made the outer display much less usable than it should be with that silly permanent dock. I also use my phones left-handed.”

“During a vacation in Morocco, we spent a night camping in the Sahara Desert. I was extremely careful with the phone and tried to avoid using it in the sand altogether. However, on the second day, when I opened it inside the tent, I heard a crunching sound coming from the hinge. Sand had somehow gotten inside. I tried everything I could to clean it, but nothing worked. The inner display was still functioning perfectly, but the phone would no longer open all the way. Even worse, when I tried to close it, I had to force it shut.”

For me personally, it couldn’t be my only phone, given the priority I place on the device as a camera, but I am still lusting after it. Given the continued extended delivery times – with random checks showing shipping in late January – I don’t think Apple has much to worry about here.

Black Friday is still a couple of weeks away, with the big shopping event falling on November 27, but Amazon's early Black Friday sale is already bringing some worthwhile discounts on Soundcore's Nebula projectors. Prices start at $299 for the compact Nebula P1i and go up to $2,799 for the premium X1S 4K laser projector, with savings of up to $700 across the models we've rounded up. There's quite a bit of variety here, too, from battery-powered projectors you can take camping or move between rooms to more powerful 4K models designed for a dedicated movie-night setup.

The Soundcore Nebula P1i is down to $299 from $399, while the Nebula P1 is $699.99, down from $799. Both offer 1080p resolution and Google TV, but their speaker setups are what make them interesting. The P1i has two 10W speakers that flip out and rotate to direct sound toward your seating area, while the P1's speakers detach completely and can run wirelessly for up to 20 hours. The P1 is also brighter at 650 ANSI lumens versus the P1i's 380, though you'll need a power outlet for either projector since neither has a built-in battery.

Small enough to slip into a bag, the Nebula Capsule 3 and Capsule 3 Laser are worth considering if you want something you can easily take on trips or move around the house. The standard Capsule 3 is down to $399 from $529, saving you $130, while the Laser version is $649.99, down from $749.99. Both offer 1080p resolution, automatic image adjustments, and up to 2.5 hours of battery life, although the Laser model is a little brighter at 300 ANSI lumens compared with the standard model's 200.

Taking movie night outdoors is a little easier with a battery-powered projector, and both the Nebula Mars 3 Air and Mars 3 are designed for just that. The smaller Mars 3 Air is down to $519.99 from $599.99, offering 1080p resolution, 400 ANSI lumens of brightness, and up to 2.5 hours of playback. The larger Mars 3, now $899.99 from $999.99, steps things up with 1,000 ANSI lumens, up to five hours of battery life in Eco mode, and a more powerful 40W speaker. It also has a weather-resistant design that's useful for camping or backyard screenings, though its extra bulk might make it less convenient to carry around.

If you're ready to move beyond 1080p, the Nebula Cosmos 4K SE at $1,099.99 (originally $1,299.99) offers a more affordable way to get 4K resolution. Its hybrid LED and laser light source delivers up to 1,800 ANSI lumens, while its Dolby Vision support helps bring out more detail in compatible movies and shows. You also get Google TV and automatic image adjustments for easier setup, though it doesn't have a built-in battery, so you'll need a power outlet nearby.

At the premium end of Nebula's lineup, the X1 and newer X1S are designed for a more serious home theater setup. The X1 is down to $2,299 from $2,999, saving you $700, while the X1S is $2,799 from $3,299. Both use triple-laser technology with 4K resolution, Dolby Vision, and optical zoom, but the X1S has a considerable advantage in brightness, reaching up to 6,000 ANSI lumens compared with the X1's 3,500. That extra brightness is useful in rooms with some ambient light, but the tradeoff is louder fan noise.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

The best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

#3280. Jensen Huang resigns as CEO of Nvidia

Jensen Huang has resigned as the CEO of Nvidia following recent reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman suspected of spying for China. Here are the details.

In late October, The New York Times reported on Jensen Huang’s “close relationship” with Alice Huang, a former managing director at Singapore-based Megaspeed, whom US intelligence officials reportedly identified as a Chinese intelligence asset suspected of passing information to Beijing.

According to subsequent reports, Chinese intelligence allegedly recruited her to gather information about Jensen Huang and influence his position on selling advanced AI chips to Chinese companies. China disputes the espionage allegations, dismissing them as groundless speculation intended to smear the country.

That said, while Nvidia previously denied any impropriety in their relationship, Huang admitted last weekend to having an extramarital affair in a message to employees, saying, “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did.” He did not mention Alice Huang directly.

In the following days, concerns grew over the potential national security implications of the relationship, in addition to Nvidia seeing its stock plummet.

And while Huang remained CEO as Nvidia’s board commissioned an independent investigation into the allegations, The New York Times reported on Wednesday that he had a second extramarital affair, this time with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him.

In the hours that followed, The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board was preparing to meet to decide Huang’s future. Soon after, Semafor reported that some board members favored Nvidia CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, while other reports suggested that Huang’s daughter, Madison Huang, could eventually succeed him. Madison Huang works at Nvidia as senior director of product marketing.

Semafor also named Apple’s chief hardware officer, Johny Srouji, as a potential successor, while Bloomberg reported that Nvidia had hired an outside firm to identify candidates.

Now, Nvidia has officially announced that Huang “has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately.”

The company confirmed that Kress has been appointed interim CEO, while retaining her current responsibilities, until a permanent successor is named. The company is considering both internal and external candidates.

Nvidia also announced that Harvey C. Jones, a longtime technology executive and venture investor, has been appointed the company’s first-ever board chair.

In a statement, Jones said the board has “full confidence in Colette and the leadership team,” adding that Nvidia expects its operations, customer commitments, and product roadmap to continue without interruption.

The shareholder lawsuits over the broad-spectrum mismanagement are going to be incredible.

No succession plan. Lying to investors to cover up the CEO’s unethical and foolish behavior. Having a super-weak board of directors absent anyone with high-level relevant experience.

Nvidia did not directly address the allegations surrounding Huang in its announcement, instead thanking him for his contributions to the company over the past 33 years.

Following the Times’ Wednesday report, Nvidia shares plunged in after-hours trading, erasing the day’s 2.9% gain after two consecutive sessions of losses.

The stock continued to fall following today’s announcement, dropping more than 10% at the time of writing from Wednesday’s closing price of $173.73, bringing its total decline to approximately 35% from its October 6 record close.

How Nvidia’s stock will behave when the market opens today and in the days that follow is anyone’s guess, especially with the company scheduled to report its quarterly earnings next Tuesday, November 17.

“I was trying to push him off, so he knew that I didn’t want him to be doing that, and so then I ended up having to hit him in the stomach to get him off. I’ve never hit anyone [before] and … he said: ‘I just wanted to see your mascara run.’”

Brand discussed his relationship with Latter during an appearance on The Megyn Kelly Show in April. He admitted that his relationship with Latter had been “exploitative” and that he had “manipulated” consent. During the same interview, he described his behavior with women as “awful but lawful.”

Latter said: “If [consent is] manipulated, it’s not given. That’s not how that works. I think also [in] doing that interview, he was quite successful in distracting people … by saying, ‘It was immoral, it wasn’t illegal.’ Well, actually something illegal happened within that relationship.”

Latter was interviewed by the police in 2024, but said she was told by the Crown Prosecution Service that she would not be included in the trial, partly because of Brand’s appearance on Megyn Kelly’s show. “I was devastated by it,” she told The Sunday Times.

Latter also expressed dismay at the media organizations and people who stood by Brand. “At times, I felt angrier with these media organizations than I have with him, because he’s a monstrous person, but to be that spineless,” she said. “He couldn’t have done this for so long without these people enabling it, and disregarding the women who made complaints at the time.”

On Monday, Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison after being found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The Sun newspaper reported on Sunday that Brand has been moved to Littlehey Prison, a jail for men who have been convicted of sexual offenses.

#3278. Wu-Tang Clan, Billy Idol, Phil Collins Enter Rock Hall at All-Star Induction Ceremony

It was difficult to imagine who could possibly top Wu-Tang Clan’s performance at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction on Saturday night at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater. Following a spirited introduction from Chris Rock, all living members of the Staten Island hip-hop group hit the stage to perform a medley of some of their biggest hits, including “C.R.E.A.M.” and “Wu-Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit.” The audience was on its collective feet screaming “Wu-Tang! Wu-Tang!” repeatedly as the mighty crew wielded their lyrical swords.

But then came the Red Hot Chili Peppers, who were part of Rick Rubin’s induction. Cosplaying Rubin (who, after an incredibly theatrical induction speech by Neil Young, accepted his honor in shorts, sandals and rose-tinted sunglasses), Anthony Kiedis, John Frusciante, Flea and Chad Smith erupted into their Blood Sugar Sex Magik single “Give It Away” donning fake white beards. After a short technical issue with Flea’s instrument, the ever-limber bassist and Kiedis continued to somehow defy aging and rocked it like it was 1991.

The high octane performances kept coming at a dizzying pace. The speeches were long (sans Rubin) and the event as usual ran well over four hours. But as Wu-Tang Clan and Rubin joined fellow honorees Queen Latifah, New Order/Joy Division, MC Lyte, Billy Idol, Iron Maiden, Luther Vandross, Sade, Oasis, Phil Collins, Celia Cruz, Fela Kuti, Gram Parsons, Linda Creed, Arif Mardin and Jimmy Miller, the excitement of “what’s next” made time disappear.

Of course several inductees opted not to show up (Oasis, New Order’s Bernard Sumner, Gillian Gilbert and Stephen Morris, Sade and Iron Maiden) and some of them were being inducted posthumously, but the Rock Hall was still able to make the evening magical with surprise presenters and performances.

U2 opened the show with “Silencio,” the lead single from their latest album, Carnaval de Luz, and their 1984 hit “Pride (In the Name of Love).” Jack Black joined St. Vincent, Metallica’s Kirk Hammett and Robert Trujillo and Rage Against the Machine’s Brad Wilk for an Iron Maiden tribute. MC Lyte came out firing on all cylinders for a cover of DJ Jazzy Jeff and the Fresh Prince’s “Boom! Shake the Room” before she was joined by Queen Latifah for “U.N.I.T.Y.” and “Ladies First” featuring Megan Thee Stallion and Remy Ma. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

Usher sailed through Luther Vandross’ hits “So Amazing,” “Here and Now” and “Never Too Much” and blossoming British chanteuse Sienna Spiro had the nearly impossible task of covering Sade’s “Smooth Operator.” With her raspy vocals and slow, sensuous execution, it worked, though there was a sense nobody would have wanted to trade places with her.

Blink-182’s Travis Barker inducted the ailing Phil Collins. He talked about the immense impact Collins had on him as an aspiring drummer, saying, “He wasn’t just an incredible drummer. He was also a singer-songwriter and one of the biggest solo artists in the world. Songs like ‘Sussudio,’ ‘Take Me Home,’ ‘Easy Lover’ and ‘Against All Odds’ was the soundtrack to my childhood. And then there’s ‘In The Air Tonight,’ his first solo single with arguably the most badass drum fill of all time. You don’t even have to be a drummer to know that fill. When that part comes on, everybody plays air drums.”

With a cane and the aid of an assistant, Collins made his way to the stage and was greeted by a standing ovation. The 75-year-old appeared more feeble than anticipated, making the moment even more emotional. “I’m really not as bad as it looks,” he quipped. “I’m much better.” Related Content Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony to Kick Off as Planned Amid FAA Grounding Flights Debacle Iron Maiden’s Nicko McBrain Recalls Spinal Tap Moments Touring for ‘Somewhere in Time’ John Mulaney Has Many Thoughts on the 2026 Rock Hall Inductees — And Picks Next Year’s Class 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame: 10 Burning Questions About Oasis, Sade, Phil Collins, and More

Collins then gave a tearful speech about his life and career, saying, “I grew up just wanting to play the drums. Everything else has been a really happy accident. I can’t believe, when I look back, how life has gone.” He also addressed the whisperings of an upcoming tour. While he didn’t confirm it would (or even could happen), he did end with, “You haven’t heard the last of me yet. I can promise you that.” Collins was unable to perform, but Cynthia Erivo did her best rendition of “In the Air Tonight” with Barker behind the kit.

Oprah Winfrey was on deck to induct Vandross. She spoke about her personal connection to the singer, saying, “Luther always gave me great counsel and taught me a lot about what it means to live well. Used to tell me, ‘Girl, use all your good dishes for yourself.’ One of my favorite songs that I heard for the first time as I was leaving my studio in Chicago, really late one night, someone on my team had handed me a new cassette tape, and I put it in for the drive home.”

“Yes, it was the eighties when cars had cassette tapes, and it was a brand-new Luther Vandross tape. And when his smash hit song ‘Power of Love’ came on, I was already almost at my front door. But I kept driving around the block, driving around the block, around the block to hear it over and over again. I love that song, still do.”

She compared listening to “Power of Love” as a “spiritual experience,” adding, “Luther Vandross was somebody who sang with such passion and soul; it could reach something deep inside that you didn’t even know was waiting to reach.”

It felt like déjà vu when Trent Reznor stepped up to the mic to induct Joy Division and New Order. Seven years ago, the Nine Inch Nails maestro welcomed the Cure into the esteemed Hall and admitted he’d been “ambivalent” about “certain award ceremonies.”

But there he was in his thick, black-rimmed glasses recounting the history of both bands. Moments later, Peter Hook stood alone at the podium without Sumner, Gilbert or Morris, making it painfully clear the band was unable to put their differences aside.

“Now I’m here and I realize how special it is,” Hook said. “It’s like being part of a family, which I’m delighted about. Now I’m on my own, but I’m not alone … it’s been a wild 50 years, and I’ve been happy, I’ve been mad and I’ve been heartbroken in equal measures. But I’m still fucking here.” Hook then picked up his bass and joined Deftones and Chvrches’ Lauren Mayberry for “Love Will Tear Us Apart” and “Bizarre Love Triangle” with the same fervor he’s harnessed for decades.

The Oasis segment, however, was a sore spot. Liam and Noel Gallagher already declined the invitation, so their absence was expected. But Stephen Wilson Jr., a country artist with no ties to British rock whatsoever, performing “Wonderwall” almost felt like a slight to Oasis. Wilson knew it, too. Backstage in the press room, he was reminded that the Gallagher brothers will likely see the performance and there was a chance they’d roast him for it. He said he had “thick skin” and would be “honored” if he were to become the target of a Gallagher brothers’ joke, but coupled with the awkward introduction by Better Call Saul actor Bob Odenkirk (who satirized the Gallagher brothers’ “cheeky” attitudes for the HBO comedy series Mr. Show in the 1990s), it seemed like Oasis’ absence was just too massive of a hole to fill.

That’s not to say the Rock Hall didn’t try: Billy Idol was ushered into the Hall by No Doubt’s Gwen Stefani and Tony Kanal. Stefani called Idol’s music a “time machine” and recalled listening to him in the early 1980s. Idol’s speech didn’t fail to entertain either as he sometimes struggled to read the teleprompter.

“Rock & roll says we can be heroes,” Idol said. “In my case I called myself Billy Idol so I could be my own hero.” He and longtime guitarist Steve Stevens proceeded to perform “Rebel Yell” and “Eyes Without a Face” as a duet with Stefani.

In the press room, Idol didn’t field any questions but posed for the cameras with his signature lip snarl and fist pumps, though Stevens spoke at length.

“Music is such a universal thing that I got the opportunity at some point to stay at Billy’s parents’ house and got to see his record collection, his adolescent William Broad record collection, and they were a lot of the same records that I grew up on,” Stevens said. “We’re roughly the same age, so it was David Bowie, T. Rex, Slade, Sweet Reed. We grew up [differently], but the music and things that inspired us were very much the same.”

Stevens also talked about his hopes for future generations of rock stars, saying, “There’s not that many true rock stars around to replace a Billy Idol. Hopefully, we’ll inspire people, and there’ll be another Steve Stevens … I’ve seen them on YouTube playing the solo for ‘Rebel Yell’ and sometimes playing it better than I can, so hopefully that’s the next generation. From what I understand, a lot of the record companies are looking at, you know, ‘Wow, we really have to develop artists again,’ because just having the numbers of viewers on TikTok or something is not a career.”

The crescendo of the evening came as Public Enemy’s Chuck D, with his inimitable and commanding voice, introduced Aerosmith to the stage. Steven Tyler, Joe Perry and the rest of the band started playing the first few notes to “Walk This Way” before Tyler suddenly stopped and told Perry there was “something missing.” Just as they’d done at The Hollywood Bowl two weeks ago, Run and DMC appeared from opposite sides of the stage to perform the crossover smash, elating the crowd.

While the 2026 iteration of the annual ceremony was mostly a success, a few things were glossed over. Gram Parsons and Ed Sullivan’s segments felt incomplete. Rumors Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr were somehow involved with the Sullivan induction ran rampant backstage, considering the Beatles’ rich history with The Ed Sullivan Show, it would have made sense. But alas, it came and went without much fanfare. Trending Stories ‘SNL’ Cold Open: Jensen Huang, Tech CEOs Get a Crash Course in Female Spies ‘SNL’ Weekend Update Roasts Trump Admin Over Grounded Flights, Jensen Huang Affairs Could ‘Rubber Soul’ Be the Best Beatles Album? (Yes) ‘SNL’: Watch Phoebe Bridgers Perform ‘Bobby,’ ‘Still Standing’

The In Memoriam portion paid tribute to a long list of musical figures we’ve lost, including Afrika Bambaataa, Rob Base, producer Bob Power, Traffic’s Dave Mason, ZZ Top’s Frank Beard and the Grateful Dead’s Bob Weir, who deserved much more than a photo flashing across a screen. Dolly Parton, however, was allotted a significant highlight reel, capturing the magic that made Dolly Dolly.

But the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame exists to ensure they are remembered long after they are gone. It’s not perfect and maybe they don’t always get it “right.” Gene Simmons may still be infuriated that hip-hop and R&B are welcome. Iron Maiden still might scoff at the idea as a whole. The Gallagher brothers might stick up their middle fingers. But still, it goes on — what’s more rock and roll than that?

#3277. Mount Thor raises $45 million to build Mac data centers for AI agents

Apple @ Work is exclusively brought to you by Mosyle, the only Apple Unified Platform. Mosyle is the only solution that integrates in a single professional-grade platform all the solutions necessary to seamlessly and automatically deploy, manage & protect Apple devices at work. Over 45,000 organizations trust Mosyle to make millions of Apple devices work-ready with no effort and at an affordable cost. Request your EXTENDED TRIAL today and understand why Mosyle is everything you need to work with Apple.

Mount Thor, a Bay Area startup building cloud infrastructure on Apple silicon, announced today that it has raised $45 million across Seed and Series A rounds. The pitch to its investors was simple: AI agents are incredible on Apple silicon, and nobody is renting them at data-center scale.

About Apple @ Work: Bradley Chambers managed an enterprise IT network from 2009 to 2021. Through his experience deploying and managing firewalls, switches, a mobile device management system, enterprise grade Wi-Fi, 1000s of Macs, and 1000s of iPads, Bradley will highlight ways in which Apple IT managers deploy Apple devices, build networks to support them, train users, stories from the trenches of IT management, and ways Apple could improve its products for IT departments.

CRV and Conviction co-led the Series A. Chad Byers and Offline Ventures co-led the Seed. CSC Leasing, Enea Capital, Long Journey Ventures, and Upper90 participated, along with angel investors from OpenAI, Meta, Cognition, Together AI, and Vercel. The company also raised separate non-dilutive financing for new hardware as well.

Mount Thor runs macOS on Apple silicon as elastic compute instances, just as a cloud provider rents Linux VMs. Customers get on-demand fleets of Macs for work that only happens on macOS: training computer-use models in reinforcement learning environments, running secure macOS sandboxes for agents, long-running instances that let an agent work across a user’s devices under one Apple ID, and build and test farms for Apple software.

There are two ways to use its solution. With managed compute, customers pick a machine class and image, and get either a full bare-metal Mac or an isolated macOS VM with administrator access, provisioned through a web portal, a command-line tool, Kubernetes, or the API, and billed per Mac on a 24-hour basis. With customer-managed compute, an organization runs its own Macs at a Mount Thor site using its own MDM, while Mount Thor operates the facility and provides inventory by serial number, problem reporting, and event notifications.

The argument is that agents are becoming macOS users, and the demand for Apple’s platform now scales with the number of agents rather than the number of people.

“Making Apple’s operating system and silicon available at datacenter-scale is a massive untapped opportunity in AI infrastructure,” said Peter Voell, Founder and CEO of Mount Thor. “Decades of investment in accessibility and human-computer interaction make macOS the best place for agents to work and for humans to hold them accountable. And with chips like the M5 Ultra, Apple silicon is becoming a high performance, more power- and cost- efficient platform for production inference.”

The other half of its pitch is inference. The M5 Ultra Mac Studio shipped in August with up to 512GB of unified memory, which puts large open-weight models within reach of a single machine at a fraction of the power draw of a traditional GPU-based server. Mount Thor says a focus of the new funding is building what it calls the best inference lab for open-source models on Apple silicon.

“Mount Thor sits at the intersection of two important shifts: the rapidly expanding capabilities of autonomous agents and the increasing demand for compute that can support both local and cloud workloads,” said Brittany Walker, General Partner at CRV. “We’re thrilled to back Peter and the team as they make it easier to use Apple’s platforms at scale for agentic AI.”

The team comes from Cerebras, CoreWeave, Fluidstack, Nebius, OpenAI, and xAI. The company was founded this year and deployed its first data center in under six months.

Macs in the cloud are not new as AWS has rented Mac instances for a few years, and MacStadium has been doing so longer than AWS. Mount Thor’s pitch is that the larger customer is an AI agent that needs a Mac to do its job, and that demand grows with the number of agents rather than the number of developers.

The company says the funding will go toward expanding its compute footprint and building out the team, and that it plans to add capacity quickly to keep up with customer demand.

#3276. Top Wall Street analysts prefer these dividend stocks for boosting portfolio returns

Dividend stocks remain a popular choice for investors seeking steady income and higher portfolio returns. However, with thousands of dividend-paying companies to choose from, identifying the right stocks can be challenging.

In this regard, recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can provide useful insights and help identify dividend stocks backed by solid fundamentals and with attractive upside potential.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Independent oil and natural gas company Permian Resources (PR) is this week's first dividend stock. The company recently paid a quarterly base cash dividend of 16 cents per share. At an annualized dividend of 64 cents per share, PR offers a dividend yield of 3.5%.

Recently, Evercore analyst Chris Baker initiated coverage of Permian Resources stock with a price target of $25. The analyst believes that the company is well positioned to benefit from improving U.S. shale demand after the Iran conflict, thanks to its low-breakeven inventory that can boost free cash flow growth. Baker also noted PR's disciplined consolidation in the Permian Basin.

Furthermore, the 5-star analyst highlighted the company's focus on a single basin and management's efficient capital allocations across expansion efforts, strategic acquisitions, and share buybacks. Baker noted that management focuses investments on the higher-return Northern Delaware Basin, helping boost profitability.

"The key piece of our work here, and the reason we think PR deserves a higher multiple relative to more finite or less flexible shale stories, is that PR runs an acquire and exploit model," said Baker.

He explained that Permian Resources deserves a premium valuation as it continually acquires and develops new high-quality assets instead of relying on a limited inventory, a strategy that is the market is underappreciating.

Baker ranks No. 862 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 48.3%. See Permian Resources Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Valero Energy (VLO) is a manufacturer and marketer of petroleum-based and low-carbon liquid transportation fuels and petrochemical products. At a quarterly dividend of $1.20 per share, or annualized dividend of $4.80 per share, VLO stock offers a yield of about 2%.

Heading into Valero's second-quarter earnings on July 30, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on VLO stock and increased the price target to $286 from $283 to reflect updated estimates.

Specifically, the 5-star analyst raised his 2026 and 2027 earnings per share estimates to $31.42 and $23.07 from $29.42 and $21.06, respectively, while leaving the 2028 EPS estimate unchanged at $20.37. Mehta made these revisions based on several factors, including updated commodity price assumptions and changes to refining capture rates.

Despite a strong year-to-date rally in VLO stock, Mehta still finds it compelling due to his more positive refining outlook. Moreover, the analyst sees the possibility of solid estimate revisions, which could drive the stock higher. He believes that Valero is well-positioned to benefit from improving refining market conditions due to its strong position in the Gulf Coast, solid balance sheet strength, and low-cost operations.

"Additionally, we believe the company's premium asset portfolio and crude slate optionality should support capture rates and stronger cash flow generation in the near-term, ultimately supporting shareholder returns," said Mehta.

Mehta ranks No. 742 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 59% of the time, delivering an average return of 10.2%. See Valero Energy Statistics on TipRanks.

Moving on to Ovintiv (OVV), a North American oil and natural gas producer. It has solid positions in North America's premier oil basins – the Permian and the Montney. OVV offers a quarterly dividend of 30 cents per share, or an annualized dividend of $1.20 per share, implying a 2.3% yield.

Following meetings with management, RBC Capital analyst Gregory Pardy reaffirmed a buy rating on Ovintiv stock with a price target of $70, highlighting that the stock is on RBC's Global Energy Best Ideas List.

"In our eyes, the depth of Ovintiv's Montney position, streamlined portfolio, strong balance sheet and enhanced shareholder returns afford investors with an attractive valuation re-rating opportunity over time," said Pardy.

The 5-star analyst stated that his meetings with management bolstered his confidence in the company's outlook and potential to achieve a higher valuation. Pardy noted Ovintiv's transformation, with the company streamlining its portfolio from six basins (including the Uinta, Bakken and Anadarko) to two – the Montney and Permian – while enhancing the depth of its inventory.

Pardy also emphasized OVV's improved shareholder returns and solid balance sheet following the recent sale of its assets in the Anadarko Basin for $3 billion.

Pardy ranks No. 169 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 22.3%. See Ovintiv Options Trading Activity on TipRanks.

#3275. Johnny Depp Pic ‘Ebenezer’ Counts $19M U.S. Opening As Moviegoers Pinch Pennies – Sunday AM Box Office Update

SUNDAY AM: It was the best of times at the box office and it was the worst of times: Paramount’s Johnny Depp comeback movie, Ebenezer, opened to No. 1, but under the $20M where tracking had been spotting it, with $19M.

Know that this isn’t a Depp problem, as 50% of the audience came because they were fans of the 3x Oscar-nominated star. There was no rush-out factor here with Ebenezer, because… c’mon, it’s a 183 year-old story that everybody knows. Thirty-four percent of the audience came for the subject-matter plot, while 8% of ticket buyers said it was part of a franchise they loved. Also, we need to consider the fact that there’s a box office tsunami coming in with Lionsgate’s The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping next weekend, which could do $100M. Quite often, moviegoers ease their attendance the weekend before a big event film hits theaters.

Know the weekend result here isn’t a total bah-humbug for Ebenezer, as there’s still some Christmas wish left in the film: It has great audience exits with A- CinemaScore, 90% audience rating on Rotten Tomatoes, and 4.5 stars on Posttrack. There’s enough good will here for Depp’s Mr. Scrooge to find an audience over the Thanksgiving holiday and beyond, particularly among the older set, who we know is slow to come out and are returning during the 2026 box office boom. Watch on Deadline

Also for the pic’s net $38M production, this opening isn’t bad particularly given the fact that Christmas movies paynoff like Domaine de la Romanée-Conti wines in the long run for a major studio’s library. Depp took a $5M upfront fee, which is lower than his previous $20M average, as well as a back-end tied to the profit of the Emma Watts production.

Also realize that this movie in its old IP would have probably opened at this domestic level had it hit screens before the Depp-Amber Heard court trials. It’s not like this is a Johnny Depp non-franchise movie starring Timothée Chalamet and directed by Tim Burton.

Underscoring how older skewing this property is, the definite recommends on the Screen Engine/Rentrak PostTrak audience exits increased as each demo set got older from 10-12 year olds at 33% to 50% 18-24, 65% 25-34, 64% 35-44, 69% 45-54 to a huge high of 78% for the over 55 set. That tells you the type of picture Ebenezer is catering to with 54% over 35 and 34% over 45.

Saturday’s $7.1M off the pure Friday (sans previews) of $5.2M was +35%, which indicates there was some bump from families attending, which only repped 10% of the overall audience. Moms (essentially Depp fans) showed up at 65% with a 65% definite recommend, though Dads at 35% gave the Ti West-directed take of the Charles Dickens novella an 82% definite recommend. With genre fans not plentiful enough on this movie with 18-34 at 40%, the hope is that families might fill the void. The only thing here is that the nag factor from kids under 12 is low with 47% giving the PG-13 movie a must-see right away.

Gotta give credit to Paramount Global Marketing and Distribution boss Josh Goldstine for a creative, sticky and clever campaign here on Ebenezer. Word is, he pitched Depp on the idea of the actor getting into character as Scrooge for San Diego Comic-Con and other public appearances (the Jack Sparrow actor also went full method for a crowd in NYC). Again, the trailer drop for Ebenezer and Depp’s appearance in San Diego was one of Comic-Con’s bigger surprises.

RelishMix pointed out that word of mouth was positive on social for Ebenezer with a near 8 out of 10 buzz rating. “There’s a tone of relief, nostalgia and collective exhale that Depp is working again, with genuine curiosity about how he’ll stack up against Scrooge royalty like Alastair Sim, Albert Finney and George C. Scott. Fans are framing ‘this role less as a comeback and more as a victory lap after a rough few years.’ Fans exclaim, ‘Johnny Depp’s return is a reminder of why he’s regarded as one of the defining actors of his generation. Johnny Depp can simply play anything.'”

The social media reach across YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and X is 395M, 6% above other family-live action titles. Activation on Ebenezer runs at 50% with a total of 81.6M fans led by Johnny Depp at 56.7M fans, Rupert Grint at 5.51M and Charlie Murphy at 463K, while the other half of the cast is not-activated.

Overall weekend looks like an estimated $91.5M, +24% which is still higher than the same frame a year ago which was $74M.
